question: What must a saved document retain, validate and migrate, and which durable-state or migration layers can be eliminated?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles hard-cut comparison; focused existing contracts and current-source adversarial probe
trigger: User explicitly requested $best-api-review audit persistence after skipping diff in the ledger.
requirements: Review all four current persistence ledger units and their materially different runtime, offline CLI, copied-demo and external-state consumers.

Preserve complete documents with primary/named roots, unknown JSON metadata, feature-owned codec versions and supported authored state; keep local undo and external application records under their existing owners.

Preserve app-owned named lineage, exact historical fingerprints, ascending target-version steps, explicit unversioned support floors, structural selection mapping and failure before document publication.
Keep ordinary editor setup and document saving independent of CLI generation or collaboration; retain v54 as the current unreleased Plate target.
Compare deletion, merger, changed API, neutral owner repair and architecture replacement before selecting the next owner; persist the audit without product implementation or publication.
evidenceReuse: Initial persistence-scope review; no earlier persistence record exists. Read the prior state decision summary, registry migration separation, single-v54 hard-cut rationale and authored live-state design. Rechecked current value publication/hydration, codecs, the actual Plate runner/preparation, all migration directory responsibilities and focused specs, export reachability, runtime/demo/CLI callers and app-owned comment/suggestion snapshots. The requested sidecar reader failed at a usage limit before supplying findings; lead source review completed the scope.
summary: Pursue a detached complete document-migration boundary: remove ordinary steps' mutable editor authority and CLI editor-per-file completion, validate before returning success, and return target identity with the complete document. Keep feature codecs, app lineage and separate history; retain v54 semantics and independent legacy-comment extraction, and privatize public V53 catalogs. The API/runtime target remains provisional pending Task design and complete-operation proof.
alternatives: Keep/configure: existing app envelopes and explicit floors avoid some misuse, but cannot remove migration callback write authority or make standalone output validation match load.

Local API repair: preflight the full chain, isolate input and validate output; valuable but insufficient alone because offline conversion still depends on installed editor lifecycle and caller-built target identity.

Delete/merge into feature value codecs: reject one universal version clock; independent feature/effect/history codecs and app schema lineage have distinct current contracts. Reuse private strict JSON mechanics.

Delete all migration infrastructure in favor of app functions: reject because exact identity checks, chain dispatch, selection mapping and runtime/CLI parity are already repeated jobs. Keep one operation, without a manager/plugin/store.

Move the current runner unchanged to Plite: reject because relocation preserves live editor and Plate-specific preparation dependencies. Move only neutral document/schema/selection laws into their canonical owner.

Strongest proposed architecture: one detached complete conversion bound to exact target schema and explicit format policy; preflight, transform, prepare, validate, return current envelope and report, then save or load. Compare deleting automatic editor migration against retaining a thin delegate, without a second lifecycle.
Public cuts: V53 provenance/catalog exports have only internal/test consumers in current search and can become private. Keep the migration subpath and independent legacy-comment extraction job.
Universal saved editor session or Yjs-only persistence: reject because document data, runtime keys/views, undo replay and external app records have different lifetimes and compatibility laws.
proofLimits: Expected 4/reviewed 4/excluded 0/unresolved unit dispositions 0. Current-source tests pass: 39 codec/state/history tests across 4 files; 96 migration/CLI tests and 193 assertions across 8 files; one audit probe reproduces a deliberate callback write surviving a later missing-step failure, non-JSON output accepted by migrateDocument but rejected by load, and repeated raw-result migration without target identity. The probe does not show built-in v54 corruption or sandbox arbitrary application callbacks. No proposed runtime, type-inference, scale, browser, real storage backend, packed-release or publication claim. Existing type continuity proofs were inspected, not rerun. Design must preserve actual v54 schema/list/ID/authored/selection dependencies and measure complete current/candidate conversion before runtime acceptance.
